rankingCriteria: information gain, safety, cost, prerequisite readiness, and whether the outcome would change a decision. Rank 1 is highest.

items.title: Commission an independent reimplementation of the transaction evaluator
items.hypothesis: An implementer working only from the public schema, with no access to knowledge_ledger/transaction.py, will reach the same conclusion for all 176,120 exhaustive worlds.
items.discriminatingTest: Run both evaluators over the frozen exhaustive enumeration and diff conclusions world-by-world. Any disagreement localises exactly where two readings of the schema diverge.
items.whyItMatters: This single artifact unblocks TWO gates. It is KL-000's next gate (RESEARCH-METHOD.md forbids the implementation author being the sole verifier) and it is half of KL-011's two-implementation requirement. Commissioning it once serves both; commissioning it twice would be waste.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Disagreement would block KL-011 and reopen KL-000. Agreement is the precondition for any cross-system claim, and therefore for any First Transmission candidate.
items.cost: one implementation, no data, no spend, no authorization

items.title: Bind the declared search space before evidence collection so under-declaration is detectable
items.hypothesis: A receipt that commits to a search-space digest fixed BEFORE collection can detect the omission attack that constraint ADV-001 shows is currently invisible.
items.discriminatingTest: Construct two ledgers identical except that one omits the location holding the counterexample. Under the current schema both verify and only the truncated one reaches absent_within_declared_scope. Add a prior searchSpaceDigest field and show the truncated ledger now fails to verify against it.
items.whyItMatters: ADV-001 is the cheapest attack on the program's headline property: no forgery, no copies, no compromised issuer, only omission. It also arrives by accident whenever a ledger is partially delivered, since a truncated ledger and a dishonest one are byte-identical.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Determines whether bounded-absence claims are meaningful against an adversarial or lossy reporter, or only against an honest one.
items.honestLimit: This moves the trust boundary from the reporter to whoever fixes the scope. It does not eliminate it, and the backlog must not pretend otherwise.

items.title: Represent shared dependency between distinct roots
items.hypothesis: A dependency edge between rootIds allows partial dependence to be declared and collapsed, closing the half of RESEARCH-METHOD's mandatory copied-or-shared-dependency control that is currently untestable.
items.discriminatingTest: Two roots derived from one upstream source, declared with a dependency edge, must not yield margin 2.
items.whyItMatters: Blocks KL-006 and KL-008 substantively, not incidentally. Dependency structure IS the subject of KL-006, and one instrument feeding many derived products is exactly this structure in KL-008. Both kernels would produce meaningless results under v0.1.
items.cost: schema v0.2, evaluator change, new invariants, new controls
items.note: An evaluator change reopens KL-000: the frozen evaluator hash would no longer match, so KL-000 must be re-run against the new evaluator under a new protocol version.

items.title: Make every agent-reported provenance field independently captured or explicitly marked unverified
items.hypothesis: Provenance fields an agent reports about its own execution context are unverifiable from inside that context and drift silently.
items.discriminatingTest: For each provenance field, ask whether an independent capture exists. This run produced two failures of exactly this kind within one session: PROV-004 (a transcription digested as the original prompt, found only by an operator's earlier independent capture) and PROV-005 (a deleted remote's cache measured and reported as the remote).
items.whyItMatters: Both failures were internally consistent, self-digesting, and wrong. Neither could have been caught by re-reading. They are the same error the program's copy-invariance invariant exists to prevent, occurring in the provenance layer where no invariant was checking.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether any run's provenance record can be relied on at all.
items.proposal: run-manifest.json carries a capture method per field: operator-file, harness-capture, or agent-transcription. The last marks the field unverified and the run provenance-incomplete. Ideally the harness writes prompt bytes to disk before the agent starts.
items.cost: harness change plus a manifest field

items.title: Preregister the intended branch-exercise profile alongside randomized bounds
items.hypothesis: Declaring which evaluator branches a randomized phase should exercise, and in what proportion, surfaces sampling skew before execution rather than after.
items.discriminatingTest: KL-000's randomized phase drew sides per-record over 8 roots and up to 24 records, making side conflict near-certain: 75.7% of worlds failed closed and never produced a receipt, so eight of ten invariants were exercised on 243,381 worlds rather than 1,000,000. Draw sides per-root instead, or stratify, and confirm the receipt-producing fraction matches a declared target.
items.whyItMatters: The headline 'one million worlds' overstated the randomized phase by roughly a factor of four for most invariants. The result stands, but its size was misdescribed until decomposed.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Does not change KL-000's verdict; changes how large a randomized phase must be to claim a given bound.
items.cost: generator change plus a preregistration field

items.title: Emit the evidence-ledger fields RESEARCH-DIRECTION.md requires but the receipt omits
items.hypothesis: flipBudget, unattributed evidence, and uncertainty are specified as evidence-ledger contents but never emitted, so they cannot be shown to survive crossing systems.
items.discriminatingTest: Add them to the receipt and include them in KL-011's protected-field set.
items.whyItMatters: KL-011's acceptance gate requires protected fields to survive five stages. A field the reference receipt never carries is trivially and vacuously 'preserved'.
items.cost: evaluator change; reopens KL-000 as in BL-003

items.title: Specify root-identity normalisation, or declare byte identity as intentional
items.hypothesis: Unspecified normalisation makes root splitting deniable: a zero-width space or a case change splits one source into two roots with no forgery and a plausible data-entry explanation.
items.discriminatingTest: Preregister a normalisation rule (NFKC plus case folding plus whitespace stripping, or explicitly none) and show near-identical rootIds collapse or provably do not.
items.whyItMatters: ADV-004 is ADV-002's sybil attack made deniable, and it costs an attacker nothing.

items.title: Decide whether side-conflict should reject a transaction or quarantine the conflicting root
items.hypothesis: Quarantining the conflicting root preserves availability without producing a wrong answer, where whole-transaction rejection lets one appended record suppress a valid conclusion.
items.discriminatingTest: Implement quarantine as an alternative evaluator and check that no invariant is violated under the KL-000 suite, then compare adversary cost.
items.whyItMatters: ADV-003: fail-closed is correct for truth and free for the adversary who wants silence. Governing principle 8 says uncertainty causes abstention; here an adversary manufactures abstention on demand.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether the system is deployable where availability matters.
items.caution: Quarantine risks discarding a genuine counterexample recorded under a colliding rootId. The comparison must include that failure mode, not only the availability gain.

items.title: Migrate KL-001..KL-011 preregistrations from schema v0.1 to v0.2
items.hypothesis: v0.1 cannot express four of RESEARCH-METHOD's twelve required fields, so no v0.1 preregistration can satisfy the method however fully it is populated.
items.discriminatingTest: scripts/audit_preregistrations.py reports zero 'NO SCHEMA KEY' findings after migration.
items.whyItMatters: Blocks the program-success criterion that every kernel have a complete preregistration. Currently unsatisfiable rather than merely unsatisfied.

items.title: Test whether the four-layer separation holds for build provenance and software supply chain
items.hypothesis: Ground source, evidence method, independent reproduction, and durable history separate cleanly in reproducible-builds attestation, where an independently rebuilt artifact is a genuinely independent root and a signed attestation is not.
items.discriminatingTest: Take a package with N signed attestations from one builder and M independent rebuilds. Show root counting distinguishes them where signature counting does not.
items.whyItMatters: Suggested by evidence rather than by analogy: this domain already has the ground-source/durable-history confusion the program describes, since signatures are routinely counted as corroboration. It also has public immutable fixtures and needs no human subjects.
items.priorArtWarning: in-toto, SLSA, and reproducible-builds literature must be reviewed as primary sources before any novelty is claimed.

items.title: Enforce the run's own methodology notes mechanically rather than by intention
items.hypothesis: Articulating a discipline does not produce it. Mechanical enforcement does.
items.discriminatingTest: A pre-push hook rejecting history rewrites on research branches, and an audit check that a preregistration's last-modifying commit equals its PROTOCOL-COMMIT.txt sidecar.
items.whyItMatters: This run wrote methodology note M2 -- warning that amending makes an amendment log unfalsifiable -- and then amended a reviewed results commit two commits later (PROV-007). The gap between stating a principle and following it was invisible from the inside and was caught only by an operator.

items.title: Resolve the 887bd2f / github-main divergence
items.hypothesis: The reference-rendering work on agent/first-transmission and the decision-quality clarification on github/main are independent and can be merged without conflict.
items.whyItMatters: Two commits each way past merge-base 1d1491e, touching 10 files. Not urgent -- knowledge_ledger/transaction.py is byte-identical on both sides, which this run verified by reproducing KL-000 from the github/main base.
items.note: Separate PR under the one-question-per-PR rule. Explicitly NOT done by this run, per operator instruction.
